body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA) (CEO Hyun Woo Kim) said on the 27th that it generated more than three times the business outcomes compared with the previous year by operating the 743-square-meter “Seoul Pavilion” at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 (Tuesday) to 9 (Friday).

According to the SBA, Seoul startups that participated in the Seoul Pavilion won 17 CES Innovation Awards (including one Best of Innovation), held 1,759 business meetings with global companies and institutions, and signed 30 technology cooperation MOUs during CES 2026. Compared with the previous year, on-site business meetings increased by more than 41 percent per company on average, while the number of agreements rose more than threefold overall, indicating a clear increase in both volume and intensity.

SBA attributed these results to its structured, step-by-step support program that connects pre-exhibition preparation, on-site operations, and post-event follow-up. Beginning six months before the exhibition, SBA provided one-on-one consulting to participating companies to prepare for the Innovation Award. At CES, SBA arranged in advance business matching with global buyers and venture capital firms, operated an in-house media center for global promotion, and assisted with on-site interviews. After CES, SBA plans to continue follow-up support to ensure consultations and MOU outcomes translate into actual contracts and other tangible results.

Centered on SBA as the lead organizer, the Seoul Pavilion implemented an expanded industry-academia-government collaboration model compared with the previous year, with participation from four district offices (Gangnam District Office, Gwanak District Office, Guro District Office, and Geumcheon District Office), five startup support organizations (Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Social Venture Hub, Seoul Fintech Lab, Seoul AI Hub, and Campustown Growth Center), and nine major Seoul-based universities (Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kwangwoon University, Sogang University, Seoul National University, Sungkyunkwan University, Yonsei University, Ewha Womans University, and Chung-Ang University).

body.cap: A group photo of participants, including presenters, award recipients, and judges, at the Global Innovation Forum. | Image by Seoul Business Agency

body.x: In particular, SBA said it showed a new model for cross-border business cooperation and global networking through the Global Innovation Forum, held on the second day of the CES exhibition, with cooperation among seven countries centered on Seoul.

The forum was held to foster collaboration among startup support organizations from seven countries. Alongside the SBA as host, TTA, S-GE, the Israel Economic and Trade Office, JETRO, the Quebec Government Office, and Business France participated to strengthen efforts to build a cross-country collaboration ecosystem.

A total of 237 industry stakeholders and pavilion operators from 16 countries attended the forum, including the seven partner countries. SBA said more than 100 people from global media outlets such as Geekazine and Digitimes, as well as global venture capital firms including Plug and Play and Angel AI, participated and drove strong on-site interest as a startup-centered international networking event.

Key programs of the Global Innovation Forum included a country-by-country representative company IR pitching competition, a panel talk session, one-minute PR and interviews, and networking. For the IR pitching competition, 26 judges from global venture capital firms, industry experts, and overseas media representatives evaluated companies based on criteria including global scalability, technological competitiveness, and investment appeal. As a result, FIRSTHABIT won the Grand Winner award, Hua Tech International received the Scale-up Award, and CubicSpace earned the Impact Award.

body.cap: Hyun Woo Kim, CEO of the Seoul Business Agency, delivers opening remarks at the Global Innovation Forum. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In the panel discussion that followed, startup support organizations from each country shared their startup policies, investment ecosystems, and global expansion strategies, and discussed the possibility of establishing channels for cross-country cooperation that would continue beyond CES. One participating company said, “The Global Innovation Forum served as a stage where CES participating companies could actually verify their potential for global cooperation,” reflecting on the experience.

Hyun Woo Kim said, “This CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion went beyond exhibition and promotion. We prepared step by step thoroughly, from pre-consulting and business matching, to open real business opportunities and contribute to company growth, and those efforts led to strong outcomes.”

He added, “In particular, the Global Innovation Forum held its second edition and advanced into a new platform that helps startups pursue global expansion and enables collaboration among startup ecosystems from seven countries,” and said, “Based on these results and experiences, we will continue expanding support so that Seoul startups can generate diverse outcomes on the global stage.”
